readme.what: Design-handoff values, extracted from wayfinder/design_handoff_pond/. A CACHE, not a spec.
readme.generated: GENERATED FILE — do not hand-edit. Any edit is overwritten on the next run.
readme.sourceOfTruth: The .dc.html boards remain the source of truth. When this file and a board disagree, THE BOARD WINS: regenerate, and take the board value.
readme.guard: src/__tests__/board-values.test.ts re-runs the extraction and fails if this file differs, so it cannot silently drift from the handoff.
readme.whyNotABrowser: Geometry comes from the inline `style` attribute, never from a computed layout — the handoff frames render under a CSS transform, so a measured rect lies about every number. Component values come from running each .dc.html logic class’s renderVals() with a stub base class: the style objects it returns ARE the spec.

howToRead.components: components[Name].base.vals is the full element inventory at every prop default — one entry per element the component can draw (`block`, `eyebrow`, `thead`, …), each a style object, plus the fixture text and the `isKind` flags that say which elements a kind actually renders.
howToRead.variants: components[Name].variants["kind=table|theme=ink"].delta is a DELTA against base.vals. It is a delta because renderVals returns every element’s style for every kind (the template picks with sc-if), so the resolved copies are ~98% identical — and the delta is the actual answer to "what makes this kind different".
howToRead.states: variants[…].states["hover"] is a delta against THAT VARIANT’s resolved vals (not against base). An empty object means the state changes nothing at this level, because the change lives in a child component the variant imports — e.g. PondBlock hover moves one row into PondMolecule state=hover, which is in that row’s own entry.
howToRead.secondary: variants[…].secondary["size=mobile"] is the same delta form, against the same variant, for the axes not crossed in full (size, level, color, role).
howToRead.resolve: resolved(variant) = deepMerge(base.vals, variant.delta). resolved(state) = deepMerge(resolved(variant), states[state]). Keys a delta omits are unchanged.
howToRead.deltaConventions: In a delta: `null` means the key is absent in that state, and { "__arrayPatch": { "1": … } } patches index 1 of a same-length array (other indices unchanged). A whole array is given verbatim when its length changed.
howToRead.unsetProps: unsetProps are props the extractor leaves unset on purpose, so each component’s own `p.x ?? "…"` fallback fires — that fallback is the designer’s fixture copy, which is more informative than the editor default (usually an empty string). Pass your own value for these.
howToRead.boards: boards[Name].frames[] carries the board’s own frame id (`2i`, `3a`, …), its data-screen-label, its caption prose (the rule that frame commits to), the frame root style, every <dc-import> usage — which is the board’s record of exactly which component variants it shows — and every styled element with its inline style and its own text.

readme.findingAValue: jq '.components.PondBlock.variants["kind=table|theme=ink"]' wayfinder/board-values.generated.json — or just grep the variant key: the layout keeps each element’s whole spec on one line, so one hit gives you all of its values.
readme.units: Values are verbatim. A bare number in a component style object is a React style number (px for lengths, unitless for fontWeight/lineHeight/opacity/flex); board values are raw CSS strings, so property names there are kebab-case. Nothing is rounded, snapped to a token, or reconciled with prose elsewhere — 13.5 means 13.5px.

elements.text: What a page says. Grouped because they share the page registers: serif for prose, sans for headings.
Labels a group or a column.
Text that lives on a page. Serif 200.
A kept passage. Wheat under ink.
A field name, a formula, a path.
What a record holds. Grouped because each is a field type on a database, with its own parsing and its own error.
A chip that opens the record.
What you drop in. Grouped because they upload, load and fail the same way.
A still with one play mark.

A choice made before a save.
Text that lives on a page. Serif 200.

empty, link a record, drop an image, in 68% ink. Never a dash that looks like data.

elements.text: What organisms repeat: a block repeats rows, cards or entries; a picker repeats menu rows.

A dot, a title, one value. The unit of every list.
A checkbox and a step. Done is struck in 68%.
Atoms in columns. A deleted relation breaks in place.
A record as a card: image, title, tag, one value.
A dated line of prose. The unit of a journal or a log.
A label and a value on a record page.
What Pond says: each marks something Pond did, found or is waiting on. Mono, never prose.
A calm line about something that happened, with one way to act.
Where a value or a claim came from. Opens the source.
One change in a proposal. Removals struck, sign in red.
The one floating note a date field sends.
One record on a board. Title, due date, steps done. Dragging it between columns changes its status field.

A molecule holds atoms and controls; it never restyles them. Change an atom and every row that uses it follows.
A list row lists, a card shows a record, an entry records a moment. If it needs two jobs, it is two molecules.

elements.text: Before anything is typed: the last three pages, then two actions Pond expects from the time and the page you are on.
Pages, then records, then actions. A page matched by its content says so under its name. Matched letters are underlined; there is no highlight colour.
A leading > drops pages and records. Every action is a page action underneath, so the list is the same set the / menu and the handle offer.
Records are first class. Opening one goes to its record page; the line under it shows the field that matched.
No dead end. The first row asks Pond in the composer, the second makes the page, and a close spelling is offered last.
Opening ⌘K with a page selected in the rail scopes it to that page and its children. ⌫ on an empty line clears the scope.
Full width near the top, over the dimmed page. Keys shrink to the two a phone keyboard can use.
Pages, records and actions share one list and one set of keys. The order is fixed so the eye learns where to look.
Same glass as the composer, placed high on the screen. The page behind is washed back so the palette reads as a pause, not a panel.
Actions that change a page open their own diff or page. The palette only navigates and starts things.

frames.label: 2f composer
frames.caption: organism · the composer. from one line to a thread with a diff in it. PondComposer, props: state, theme, size. Diff lines and buttons are PondMolecule and PondControl.

elements.text: One line over the page. It holds a question, / for blocks, or @ for a page. Send stays grey until there is something to send.
An @-mention becomes a chip in the line, so it is clear which page the question is about. ↵ sends; ⇧↵ adds a line.
The thread grows upward from the line. The answer is set in the sans at reading size. Send turns into stop while it streams; esc also stops it.
Under the answer, the pages it read, each one a link. Make this a page is the only way an answer reaches a page; ask again replaces the answer in place.

Asking for a change returns a proposed diff inside the thread. Nothing touches the page until accept; request changes tells Pond what to revise, and reject leaves the page as it was. Red marks the rem
Past three turns, older ones fold into one line above. A header names the thread and where it started; new thread clears it, and × closes the composer back to one line.
If an answer breaks off, nothing half-written is kept. Ask again runs the same question.
Out of the way while you work on the page. Only the top edge shows at the bottom centre; the expander or ⌘J brings it back with the thread as it was.
If you collapse mid-answer, the answer keeps streaming. When it is done, the expander says so and stays that way until you open it. It never opens itself.
Full width above the keyboard. Send and the tools grow to 40px; the line is 16px so the phone does not zoom.
Questions, chips, provenance and the controls are mono. Answers are PP Neue Montreal at 15/1.6. The serif belongs to pages only.
Nothing in the thread changes the page underneath. The only ways out are an accepted diff and make this a page.
Focuses the line. esc steps back one level: stop, then blur, then close the thread.
